what_this_is: Every RED (scene, viewport) in the last recorded screenshot sweep must appear here,
filed under a defect id that exists in docs/DEFECTS.md. `./scripts/dev.sh shots-verdict`
-- which `make hygiene` runs -- fails on any red that is NOT listed, and equally on any
entry here that is no longer red.
WHY IT EXISTS. The pixel gate caught a real regression at 4af6dc6 (docs/DEFECTS.md E-63:
8.7% of a money figure covered by the felt) and NOBODY ACTED, for a whole wave. It was not
hidden: the sweep exited 1 and wrote it into the manifest. It was unreachable -- the only
thing that could see it was a sweep that needed a live replica, and the replica was down,
so no gate anyone could run was red and the finding sat in an artifact. This file makes
the LAST RECORDED VERDICT itself a gate: writing a red down is the only way past it, and
writing it down means filing a defect.
IT IS NOT A WAIVER LIST. An entry does not make a red acceptable; it makes it ACKNOWLEDGED.
The stale check is what keeps that honest: the moment a sweep comes back green for one of
these, its entry here fails the gate until it is deleted. docs/DEFECTS.md HARD RULE 7 --
a marker that pins a fixed defect is worse than no marker.
covers_added_2026_08_07_wave_12: EVERY ENTRY NOW HAS TO SAY WHAT IT IS EXCUSING. docs/DEFECTS.md E-87.
Until this wave an acknowledgement was granted per (scene, viewport). So once a shot was
red for ANY reason, every LATER failure on the same shot joined the same `problems` array
and was excused by an entry that had never been about it. That is exactly what happened:
tools/shots/lib/table-in-frame.mjs landed in wave 12 and its first real conviction -- the
Leave-table control rendering 6-7 px outside a 1440 px frame, which a player cannot reach
or scroll to (E-85) -- appeared on table-preflop/desktop and table-facing-bet/desktop.
Both were already acknowledged under E-76 for a felt shortfall of 0.2 points, and
`dev.sh shots-verdict` stayed green over a control nobody can press.
So `covers` lists the substrings of the recorded problems each entry accounts for. Every
recorded problem must match one of them, and every cover must still match a recorded
problem -- rule 2 at the level of the problem, so a cover that stops applying fails the
way a stale acknowledgement does. `defect` may be an array when a shot carries more than
one distinct failure.
WHAT WENT GREEN THIS SWEEP, measured, and is therefore deleted from this list:
E-75  table-sidepots/mobile: the pod clock over the stack figure. 'pixel gate: 26
figures on screen, 0 occluded' on the shot that carried it. FIXED ON PIXELS.
E-86  deposit/desktop and deposit/mobile: both were red in the 134550e sweep with
'DEPOSIT CHAIN DISAGREEMENT ... screen is 1.500x the chain' on a screen where
every figure was correct. The GATE was wrong, not the screen; it read the
notice's numbers positionally and the copy had grown a fourth. Both green.
went_green_2026_08_08_wave_13: E-71  handhistory/desktop and handhistory/mobile. Both were red with
'HISTORY CHAIN DISAGREEMENT: hand 1: the TABLE canister paid 2400000000 e8s but
the HISTORY canister recorded 20000000 e8s paid'. Neither figure was ever wrong:
the gate matched the table's hand to the archive's record by `hand_number`, which
restarts at 1 on every reset_table, so it was comparing two different hands. On the
local archive one such citation answered to 70 records with 6 different pots.
A hand is now named `table_id:seed_hash` -- its shuffle commitment, unique over all
3,218 archived records and derived on read, so nothing was rewritten or renumbered --
and the gate joins on that name AND ASSERTS THE JOIN: the record it compares against
must carry the name of the hand it is compared with. Both shots verified at both
viewports. Reverting the lookup to `hand_number` puts the shot straight back to red,
now reading 'JOIN BROKEN ... those are two different hands' instead of a money
mismatch, which is the difference between a gate and an alarm nobody can act on.
docs/DEFECTS.md E-71; tools/shots/test-hand-identity.mjs holds it with no replica.
